Question Paper  
Exam Date & Time: 18-Nov-2025 (02:00 PM - 05:00 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  MANIPAL INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY - BENGALURU  
  SEVENTH SEMESTER B.TECH. DEGREE EXAMINATIONS - NOVEMBER 2025  
  Ethereum Smart Contract Using Solidity [IT_4421]  
Marks: 50                                                                                                     Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  PART-A  
Answer all the questions.  
  
1)                In a blockchain network, each block contains the hash of the previous block along with the         (5)  
  transaction data. The hash value is recalculated each time a new block is added. Apply the concept  
  A)           of cryptographic hash functions to explain how they are used to maintain the integrity of the  
  blockchain. What would happen if someone tried to modify the data in an existing block?  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)           A startup is developing a secure messaging application that allows users to exchange confidential (5)  
  messages over the internet. The development team decides to use asymmetric cryptography to  
  protect message confidentiality and verify sender authenticity. Construct a security mechanism  
  using the principles of asymmetric cryptography that ensures both confidentiality and authenticity of  
  the messages exchanged between users. Explain how public and private keys would be used in  
  your design.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
2)                A blockchain-based attendance tracking system is being developed for a small organization. Each (5)  
  time an employee checks in, the counter should increment, and when they check out, it should  
  A)           decrement. The HR manager wants to use a simple Ethereum smart contract to track the number of  
  employees currently present in the office in real time. You are provided with the following Counter  
  smart contract, which maintains and updates a count value using increment and decrement  
  functions. Develop the process using this smart contract to track employee attendance. Explain how  
  the inc() and dec() functions can be used to solve the problem of real-time employee count  
  management on the blockchain.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)           A developer is testing a decentralized marketplace application but encounters an error: "Invalid ABI (5)  
  or function signature mismatch." The developer suspects the ABI file used in the front-end is  
  outdated.  
  Apply your understanding of ABI structure to explain why this error occurs and how to resolve it.  
  Describe how mismatched ABIs affect the interaction between the front-end application and the  
  deployed contract.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
3)                A DApp uses a contract that requires periodic upgrades. When a new version is deployed, the old        (5)  
  contract should deactivate itself to prevent users from interacting with outdated logic. Construct a  
  A)           mechanism using selfdestruct()/ isActive() to retire the old contract safely while ensuring that all  
  remaining funds are transferred to the new contract address.  
  Page #1

Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)               A company deploys a Voting smart contract that allows users to vote for proposals. Later, they          (5)  
  realize a bug in the vote counting logic.  
  Build a proxy-based solution that allows the contract logic to be upgraded without losing the voting  
  data stored on the blockchain. Explain how you would separate the storage and logic contracts.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
4)                       A developer sets up an Ethereum DApp using Remix IDE, MetaMask, and the Sepolia Test            (5)  
  Network. The DApp compiles correctly, but transactions fail when deployed.  
  A)               Analyse the possible causes of deployment failure by examining the configuration between Remix,  
  MetaMask, and the test network. Suggest what environmental dependencies could lead to such an  
  issue.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
  B)               A university certificate verification DApp stores digital certificates on IPFS and uses Ethereum        (5)  
  smart contracts to verify authenticity.  
  Examine how IPFS hash values (CIDs) are used to validate certificate integrity. Differentiate this  
  verification process from traditional centralized storage validation.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Analysis"  
  
5)                       A traditional escrow service relies on a middleman to hold funds until both buyer and seller fulfill    (5)  
  their obligations. A blockchain startup replaces this with a smart contract that automatically releases  
  A)               funds when conditions are met. Examine how shifting from trust in a human intermediary to trust in  
  code enhances transaction transparency and reduces fraud, but may also introduce new risks  
  related to coding errors or vulnerabilities.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
  B)               A decentralized healthcare application needs to share patient test results with authorized doctors      (5)  
  only, without exposing them publicly.  
  Develop a mechanism using encryption or off-chain storage to ensure selective obscurity while  
  maintaining verifiability of the data.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"
